title: Bounded changes and strong reductions

based_on.title: Interactions of Computability and Randomness
based_on.pages: ICM2010 survey, p. 3: the bounded-change characterization of truth-table reducibility to the halting set.

summary: Identify computably bounded revisions with truth-table and weak truth-table computation from halting, then separate bounded-use computation from Turing reducibility.
abstract: A computable sequence of membership guesses can settle without revealing when its last revision occurs. Suppose the input nevertheless gives a computable upper bound on how many revisions are possible. The halting problem can then recover the final answer by answering a predetermined finite list of questions about those revisions. Conversely, an oracle program computing from halting with a computable bound on its query positions gives guesses with a computable revision budget. Thus these bounded-change sets are exactly the sets truth-table reducible, or weak truth-table reducible, to halting. Applying this characterization to the existing diagonal set beyond all computable change bounds separates weak truth-table computation from unrestricted Turing computation.
